title: Incident skeleton generator with trace-based prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: On-call teams get flooded with PagerDuty alerts that lack prioritized context. Engineers waste time chasing noisy alerts or assembling scattered telemetry (traces, metric deltas, recent logs) before deciding remediation. The goal of this ticket is to build an "incident skeleton generator": a small service and console action that, on PagerDuty/Slack alert creation, synthesizes a concise incident artifact and creates a Linear incident with prefilled fields, recommended severity, prioritized trace snippets, top-correlated metrics, and a suggested next-step runbook. This artifact will power faster TTR and cleaner postmortems.Automation scope: - Ingest alert payloads (PagerDuty webhook + Slack alert bridge) and map to internal alert types. - Hit tracing hooks to grab top-3 related traces (span-level heuristics + score). - Query metrics/log pipeline (recent window) for delta charts and top-correlated metrics. - Run lightweight heuristic model to recommend severity (sev1/2/3) and recommended responders (code owners + oncall role). - Generate a Linear ticket skeleton with title, description, severity label, attachments (trace links, metric snapshots, relevant PRs), and an inline suggested remediation checklist.Acceptance criteria: 1) For simulated Page events, the service attaches at least one high-confidence trace and two metric snapshots in the generated Linear ticket. 2) Severity recommendation matches historical human decisions >= 80% on held-out incidents. 3) Oncall can opt to accept or edit the skeleton before full ticket creation (UI flow in Console > Alerts). 4) All created tickets include a link back to the original alert and the trace snapshot permalink. 5) No PII or customer data leaves the VPC when Private customers trigger alerts (enforced by access controls).Design notes: - Trace scoring: combine span error counts, tail latency hotspots, and novel-span detection. - Metric correlation: look for concurrent spikes within ±60s and rank by change magnitude and SLO impact. - Use an allowlist approach for which runbooks can be suggested; rank by cosine similarity of current trace signature to historical postmortem tags. - Implement as a small Go service colocated with the observability route handler; expose a REST endpoint used by the PagerDuty/Slack webhook adapter.Rollout plan: 1) Prototype in staging with synthetic alerts and a dashboard to review suggested skeletons. 2) 2-week beta with Eng-on-call only; collect feedback and revise heuristics. 3) Gradual opt-in for teams with high alert volume (console toggle).Telemetry and observability for this work: - Instrument the generator with metrics: skeleton_creation_time_ms, trace_fetch_latency_ms, severity_confidence (0-1), false_positive_rate_estimate. - Capture sampling of generated skeletons for manual review (redaction applied).Security and compliance considerations: - Must honor data residency and KMS keys for Private deployments. - Add feature-flag to disable trace inclusion for sensitive customer orgs. - Security review required before beta in production (see security_review_required).Dependencies: - Needs the tracing lookup API stabilization (ENG-27105) - Depends on alert-routing changes in alerts-adapter (ENG-28911)
